reasons: Claimed status is compliant, and for a rule that constrains a Vendor-favourable right, the absence of any audit/inspection/verification obligation running against Company is genuinely favourable to us — no redline or comment is expected or warranted.

The cited paragraphs support the rationale: p0014 imposes invoice-substantiation duties on Contractor (in our favour), and p0007(ii) requires Contractor personnel to observe Company's system-access and security policies, which is a restriction on the counterparty rather than a grant of access to our systems.
Correctly declines to insert an audit framework; adding frequency/notice/cost limits would create a Vendor right the current bargain omits, so the minimal-edit principle is respected.

The failed 'audit frequency limited' deterministic check is a plausible false signal — the regex cannot match a frequency cap where no audit clause exists — and the finding explains this rather than ignoring it.
Rationale flags the residual risk that a Statement of Work could later introduce an audit right and states the preferred position to apply, which is appropriate internal evaluation evidence.
